# `aitbc transactions send`

Send a transaction from one wallet to another.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc transactions send [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | text | — | yes | From wallet name |
| `--to` | text | — | yes | To address |
| `--amount` | decimal | — | yes | Amount to send |
| `--fee` | decimal | `0.01` | no | Transaction fee (standard chain fee) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL |
| `--type` | text | `TRANSFER` | no | Transaction type (default TRANSFER) |
| `--payload` | text | — | no | JSON payload for non-standard transaction types |
| `--use-explorer` | flag | `false` | no | Use Explorer API for status checks |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc transactions send --from <from_wallet> --to <to_address> --amount <amount>
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc transactions send --from <from_wallet> --to <to_address> --amount <amount> --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
